Contract:
A single temporary scratch file for the current SDD session — `specs/.sdd-session.md`, gitignored, not a deliverable. It lets a multi-step or multi-scope flow survive a context squeeze or a session break within the same piece of work. The kernel reads it on entry and updates it after each loaded directive. Its lifetime is controlled by one typed terminal result:
`TerminalDecision = continue | pause | complete`.
- `continue` means a known next link remains in the current chain — root → scope → module → integrated review → scaffold → execute, including another scope in dependency order. Preserve the same session; an internal handoff never closes it. - `pause` means an Approval Check, external-review wait, critic/scaffold cap, blocker, failed check, or operator choice to resume later. Preserve the same session and its working set; a pause is not completion. - `complete` is legal only after the current terminal menu records an explicit operator choice named `complete` or `finish` and the owning step has established `unfinished chained work: none`. That step runs exact `npx gennady sdd-session close` once. No inferred completion, successful intermediate artifact, merge, ticket close, empty subagent queue, or context end may call it. `close` removes only the scratch file; the durable `.gitignore` entry remains.
A live session is never silently reused for an unrelated incoming intent. The already-gathered `sdd-state` `[SESSION]` block is the current-session card. This compatibility decision is the first write barrier: before readiness, migration, glossary, journal, spec, ticket, config, or any other project mutation, compare its literal `intent`, `scale`, `working set`, and `open` fields with the incoming intent. If related continuation cannot be proved, show that card and ask exactly one operator decision: `continue existing` or `close-and-start-new` with the proposed new intent and, only for a SCALE-consuming authoring owner, the proposed scale shown. Preserve the old file while the answer is pending (`pause`). `continue existing` routes from the stored fields without calling `open`. `close-and-start-new` itself confirms the displayed new values: run exact `npx gennady sdd-session close`; only after success run exact `npx gennady sdd-session open --intent --scale ` for a SCALE-consuming authoring owner, or exact `npx gennady sdd-session open --intent ` otherwise. Never call `--help`, guess values, or use `sdd-session open` idempotence as evidence that an existing intent is compatible. A confirmed same-chain stage transition may use exact `npx gennady sdd-session set intent ""` and `npx gennady sdd-session set scale ""`; it is not a way to relabel unrelated work.
The `scale:` field carries operator-confirmed SCALE (`AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH`) for authoring routes whose depth actually changes: `project-setup`, `new-scope`, `evolve-scope`, `module-decomposition`, and `multi-scope`, routed to root/scope/module/infra/interface. Those routes confirm SCALE once and record it in the same `sdd-session open --intent ... --scale ...` call. `execute`, `recover-from-code`, `scaffold`, `reconcile`, and `critic` consume no SCALE: the router asks no SCALE question and opens a new session with intent only. A compatible existing session may retain its already-recorded scale untouched; non-consumers do not reinterpret it.
The `glossary:` section is the session's terminology anchor (`AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE`). Only the stateful orchestrator that has crossed the compatibility/open barrier may mutate it. For each accepted term, write exactly ` — ` to the regular non-symlink payload `.claude/tmp/sdd-glossary-term.txt`, then run the router's exact glossaryUpdate ToolCall; the successful tool consumes that payload. Never pass agent-produced glossary text inline. A pre-session router buffers a suggestion without writing it. Read-only critic/audit/code-review workers return `GlossarySuggestions` and never invoke this ToolCall. In compact audit/code-review output, the final `@glossary suggestions=[ — ; ...]` line is the serialization of that exact field: `[]` maps to no suggestions; each semicolon-delimited item maps byte-for-byte to one `GlossarySuggestions` item. The compatible stateful orchestrator deduplicates these against the saved glossary, presents genuinely new/conflicting terms at its next existing operator checkpoint (never opens a glossary-only Ask), and persists only accepted items through `glossaryUpdate`. Every worker dispatch receives the current saved glossary as read-only input; a direct read-only skill reads only the `glossary:` block from `specs/.sdd-session.md` when that file exists, otherwise uses an empty list. Every later mention reuses the recorded name verbatim; before introducing a new name, check this list in the saved `sdd-state` snapshot.
Router preflight runs only AFTER compatibility/open. Its readiness cases consume the existing `activeRouterState` without invoking a readiness mutation flow. Migration alone returns exactly one alias `migrationState`; the router replaces its routing input with that snapshot and never refreshes it itself. A branch journal entry is written through the already-compatible session, so no pre-session journal buffer exists and no write can land in an unrelated session.
```markdown # SDD session — intent: scale: — operator-confirmed working set: - — — glossary: - — journal: - → open: ```
